tables.name: customers
tables.comment: Fictional demo. Customer identity schema only; no personal records.

tables.name: products
tables.comment: Fictional demo. Products identified by SKU; complex variants are not modeled.

tables.name: warehouses
tables.comment: Fictional demo. Warehouses used for dispatch and returned goods.

tables.name: inventory
tables.comment: Fictional demo. One stock record per warehouse and SKU; available = on hand minus reserved.

tables.name: orders
tables.comment: Fictional demo. Customer orders can split into multiple warehouse fulfillments and partial shipments.

tables.name: order_items
tables.comment: Fictional demo. Order lines retain quantity and unit price at purchase time.

tables.name: stock_reservations
tables.comment: Fictional demo. Order lines can reserve stock across warehouses; releasing a reservation is not dispatch.

tables.name: fulfillments
tables.comment: Fictional demo. An order can split into fulfillments by warehouse and processing batch.

tables.name: fulfillment_items
tables.comment: Fictional demo. Warehouse fulfillment lines link explicitly to order lines and stock reservations.

tables.name: shipments
tables.comment: Fictional demo. Fulfillments can split into parcels; delivery status is independent of picking and packing.

tables.name: shipment_items
tables.comment: Fictional demo. Parcel lines support partial shipments rather than keeping a single tracking number on the order.

tables.name: returns
tables.comment: Fictional demo. Returns are separate from refunds; payment and refund accounting are outside this example.

tables.name: return_items
tables.comment: Fictional demo. Return lines link to shipped lines and distinguish restocking, quarantine and disposal.

scenarios.name: Order fulfillment
scenarios.description: Fictional flow: cancel if stock is insufficient; otherwise reserve, allocate and ship. Not inferred from DDL or real logs. Partial shipments, payment and delivery confirmation are outside this scenario.
scenarios.evidence: Manually authored commerce example rules, for illustration only.

steps.name: Create order
steps.description: Read the customer and products; create the order and its lines.

steps.name: Sufficient stock?
steps.description: Example condition: on_hand - reserved >= ordered quantity.

steps.name: Reserve stock
steps.description: Record reservations and confirm the order; this is not physical dispatch.

steps.name: Record parcels and dispatch
steps.description: Simplified example: dispatch this fulfillment in one step; it does not imply delivery.

scenarios.name: Return disposition
scenarios.description: Fictional return flow: request, review, receive, then restock or quarantine. Additional information loops back to review; payment refunds are excluded.
scenarios.evidence: Manually authored commerce example rules, not a real event trace.

steps.name: Provide additional information
steps.description: Update the same return request with additional details; do not create another return.
